findings.finding: The count-consistency AC greps for the full phrase 'which of the eleven concerns above' / 'which of the twelve concerns above', but the plan only quotes the source string as hardcoding 'eleven concerns' (discovery.md:152). If the actual schema text does not contain the exact longer phrase 'which of the eleven concerns above', `grep -c` returns 0 trivially and the `twelve` grep fails after the edit — a fixture/anchor mismatch (taxonomy items 1 & 4).
scenarios: The source reads 'eleven concerns' rather than 'which of the eleven concerns above'; the AC's grep -c for the long phrase returns 0 regardless of the edit and the 'twelve' grep never matches, so the AC cannot prove the count was flipped.
findings.suggested_fix: Quote the verbatim :152 sentence in the plan and grep on that exact substring (e.g. `grep -q '"twelve" concerns'` if the source form is 'eleven concerns'), rather than the unverified 'which of the ... concerns above' phrase.

findings.finding: The plan introduces 'oracle strength' as a concern and three new portable antipattern ids without grounding them in the established prior art — mutation testing / the coverage-vs-mutation 'oracle gap', and published test-smell taxonomies (tsDetect FSE'20, testsmells.org) — so a reviewer cannot tell whether the new ids repackage known classes. In particular `fixture-mutates-foreign-state` overlaps the cited rubric's own 'isolation failure — cross-test state / fixture pollution' (code-review-tests.md:76-77) and the classic 'Test Run War' / 'Mystery Guest' smells, which risks re-declaring a class the plan pledges not to duplicate.
